name: GEN-1.5
summary: GEN-1.5 loads a 3-to-12-second demonstration into the model's context window as a physical prompt, and the robot then performs the task with no gradient steps at all. Generalist emphasises that nothing in the architecture was built for this: no meta-learning loop, no auxiliary objective, no architectural change — the capability appeared out of more than eight months of continuous pretraining on physical interaction data, the way in-context learning appeared in language models. Across ten evaluation tasks including opening a jar and pulling money from a wallet, the company reports 59% average success one-shot, rising to 83% after ten training steps on five minutes of data. Generalist describes it as the first demonstration of one-shot and few-shot physical skill acquisition at scale.
innovation: Physical prompting: demonstrations as context rather than as training data, making task specification a runtime operation.
Presents in-context skill acquisition as an emergent property of pretraining scale rather than an engineered mechanism.
matters: Together with Skild S1, announced days apart, it marks the point where the field's unit of teaching shifts from a dataset to a prompt.
limits: Company announcement only; no paper, no released weights, no third-party evaluation.
Ten tasks is a narrow base for an emergence claim, and reported announcement dates vary (19-24 August 2026).
lineage: Large-scale robot pretraining carried far enough that in-context learning appears, as it did in language models.
